title: Japan's Favorite Rice Dish Is Chahan — Survey
paragraphs: Rice is an important part of Japanese food. But what is Japan's favorite rice dish? According to a new survey, the answer is chahan, or fried rice.
The survey was done by Nichirei Foods, a Japanese food company. In June 2026, it asked about 14,000 people across Japan to choose the rice dishes they like.

Chahan came first. About 69.9% of people chose it. In second place was onigiri, or rice balls, at 63.0%. Katsudon, a bowl of rice with fried pork on top, was third at 60.1%. Chahan was also the top choice in the company's surveys in 2020 and 2024.

The survey also asked people what they put in their chahan at home. In every part of Japan, people said eggs and green onions were the most important. Many people also use pork, such as sausages, ham or bacon. Green peppers, carrots and lettuce are also popular vegetables to add. Some areas have their own special ingredients. In Nara and Wakayama, some people add sweetcorn, and in Niigata, some people add clams. For example, in parts of northern Japan, some people add natto, which is made from fermented soybeans.
On average, it costs about 297 yen to make chahan at home. Tokyo was the most expensive place, at about 393 yen.
People in western Japan eat chahan most often. In Kochi Prefecture, 60.9% of people eat it at least once a month. Ehime and Shiga came next, at 59.0% and 58.7%.
